source.title: Federated Foundation Models Fine-Tuning with Heterogeneous Compressed Clients
source.authors: Sheng-Kun Zhu; Jin-Shan Zeng; Zhihua Allen-Zhao; Mayi Xu; Quanqing Xu; Wei Ren; Qiang Yang; Yang Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-to-strong refinement in a federated setting and compares an auxiliary confidence-loss variant with naive weak-imitation training, but uses benchmark accuracy rather than Burns et al.'s PGR measure.
record.gate_note: The paper does not calculate PGR or directly report the accuracy of the aggregated weak supervisor alongside the final strong student in the server-side results. The alpha=0 versus alpha=0.5 accuracy comparisons bear on the auxiliary-loss version. Client-side scores, vision-language scores, and comparisons to pretrained or federated baselines are recorded separately but do not establish student-over-supervisor performance. Theoretical derivations and cited results are not empirical result rows.
record.test_reason: In a new setting, a federated, SVD-compressed aggregated weak supervisor teaching a full LLaMA-2/LLaVA server, the study ablates the auxiliary confidence loss (α=0 vs α=0.5). Because both arms share the same weak supervisor, a higher student accuracy implies a higher PGR, so the ablation bears on V2 even though PGR is never computed. The rest of the paper uses weak-to-strong as a component and reports only its method's performance against federated baselines (T4-like). The aggregated weak supervisor Wg's accuracy is never reported, so V1 cannot be checked.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that FedSLM's two-stage aggregation plus weak-to-strong elicitation transfers federated knowledge to the server and outperforms federated baselines in IID and non-IID settings, for language and vision-language tasks. They also say the confidence loss gives a 'reliable additional gain' consistent with their artifact-attenuation theory (Proposition 3). They do not show that the student exceeds the weak supervisor.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an aggregated, SVD-compressed federated weak model to supervise the full server model, with an auxiliary self-confidence loss; compares alpha=0 with alpha=0.5 using benchmark accuracy rather than Burns et al.'s PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported contribution of the confidence-loss setting differs across IID and non-IID partitions and model scales; named benchmark gains also vary by task.

fits_no_version.finding: FedSLM server and vision-language accuracies are reported against federated baselines or the pretrained full model. Compressed-client Stage-1 accuracies are reported against zero-shot baselines. None is compared with the aggregated weak supervisor.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In federated SVD-compressed settings, weak-to-strong refinement yields server accuracies above federated baselines and above the pretrained full model; whether the student exceeds its supervisor is unreported.

record.problems: The paper reports no PGR, no direct server-side weak-supervisor versus strong-student comparison, and no uncertainty estimates for the reported accuracies. The α ablation compares accuracy rather than the claimed gap-recovery measure.
record.rows_left_out: Most per-benchmark accuracy cells in Tables II and III are not separately extracted; the four aggregate comparisons and the task-level alpha comparisons described explicitly in the text are retained. Other baseline comparisons are outside the specific weak-to-strong versions.

untested.parts: No PGR and no reported accuracy for the aggregated weak supervisor Wg. Client-side Table IV scores are per-group compressed models, not Wg, so student-over-supervisor cannot be read.
No PGR. Ensembling weak supervisors and other loss variants are not tested. No sweep of α beyond 0 and 0.5, despite the theory prescribing an optimal α.
No analysis of how weak-to-strong gain varies with supervisor or student size, compression ratio, or representations. 7B and 13B are reported, but no PGR trend is given.

There is no measurement of exploitation of the supervisor, PGR under distribution shift, or error overlap. IID vs non-IID client partition is not a train/test distribution shift of the weak-to-strong step.
The theory bounds artifact attenuation and the optimal α. It does not derive conditions under which the student must beat its supervisor.
Vision-language results lack the weak supervisor's accuracy and a strong ceiling. Only the α ablation (V2) is available there.

missing.what: α=0 vs α=0.5 accuracy on vision-language tasks. α=0: ScienceQA 70.9 IID / 71.8 non-IID, VizWiz 69.9 / 69.7. α=0.5: 71.8 / 72.7, 70.1 / 69.9.
Per-benchmark cells where α=0.5 is equal to or worse than α=0: 7B non-IID HellaSwag 76.6→76.0, PIQA 82.2→80.7, COPA and MedMCQA unchanged; 13B IID WinoGrande unchanged.
missing.locator: Tables II and III, FedSLM rows

record.verdict_notes: The implementation of the confidence loss is inconsistent. The main text defines a hardened self-prediction with an adaptive batch threshold (Eqs. 10–11). Appendix B instead describes 'entropy regularization α·H(p̂strong)' on per-choice soft targets, so what α=0.5 actually adds is unclear. The authors claim the gain is largest where 'the weak supervisor is noisier', but supervisor noise is never measured. The weak-to-strong step uses LoRA on the server. No PGR, no weak-supervisor accuracy, and no seeds or uncertainty are reported.

versions.untested_parts: No PGR and no direct server-side strong-student versus aggregated weak-supervisor comparison.
Compares the auxiliary confidence loss with alpha=0 naive weak imitation using accuracy, not PGR; does not test ensembling weak supervisors or other loss variants.
Reports results across model scales, tasks, and vision-language benchmarks, but does not measure how PGR varies with those factors or test representation predictors.
Includes IID and non-IID partitions, but does not measure PGR under distribution shift or test supervisor/student error overlap or exploitability.
Provides theoretical analysis of aggregation and artifact attenuation, not conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
Applies FedSLM to vision-language tasks and reports task accuracy, but does not compare the strong student directly with the weak supervisor or calculate PGR there.

relation.reason: Comparing α=0 with α=0.5 tests the auxiliary confidence loss rather than merely using weak-to-strong training as a component.

tranche.reason: The federated setting with heterogeneous SVD-compressed clients is new, and the confidence-loss ablation directly bears on V2.

source_check.notes: The paper reports accuracy, without numerical PGR, a true-label student ceiling, or uncertainty estimates. Its α=0 comparator is weak-imitation-only server refinement following the same federated aggregation.

statements.correction: Section III-D, Eq. (10), and Section V, Baselines: α=0 uses cross-entropy against the weak model's soft labels without auxiliary confidence loss; both arms follow federated aggregation. LLaMA-2-7B IID average accuracy: 69.9% at α=0; 71.0% at α=0.5.
statements.problem: The numbers and comparator identity are correct, but classifying FedSLM's α=0 arm as other than naive weak-label fine-tuning is misleading: it uses only weak-supervisor imitation.
